entry.question: When and where did William Hubert Ferber (born December 1869, Ohio; resided Cincinnati, Hamilton County, Ohio; married Emma Becker 1890) die?
entry.rationale: The objective's primary fact is the death date and place of William H. Ferber. His tree has no death record. He appears in the 1900 census and Cincinnati city directories through 1910; the 1910 census and Ohio death records (registered from 1908) are the highest-priority sources to consult. Hamilton County death records (some pre-1908 local records survive) and the city directories' gap after 1910 may also point to a death window. This question is the gatekeeper: its answer constrains the timeframe for the burial search.

entry.question: Where was William Hubert Ferber (born December 1869, Ohio; died Cincinnati area, date unknown) buried?
entry.rationale: The objective explicitly asks for burial location as a separate fact from the death event. Ohio death certificates (post-1908) include the name of the undertaker and sometimes the cemetery; pre-1908 Hamilton County records and funeral home records may also name the burial place. Spring Grove Cemetery (Cincinnati) is the most probable candidate given that his mother, wife, and son are all buried there. This question depends on q_001 because the death date constrains which records to search.

entry.rationale: Ohio statewide death registration began 1908. Collection 1307272 ('Ohio, Deaths, 1908-1953') has 3.5M indexed records with full certificate images. If William died after December 1907 this is the highest-probability source: it will give date, place, cause, informant, and undertaker/burial details in one record.

Collection 2128172 ('Ohio, County Death Records, 1840-2001') includes Hamilton County local death registrations predating statewide registration. If William died between 1900 and 1907, county-level records are the only Ohio vital-record source. Also covers an overlap period in case a certificate exists before the 1908 statewide index begins.

entry.jurisdiction: Cincinnati, Hamilton County, Ohio, United States
entry.rationale: The 1910 U.S. Census (taken April 15, 1910) will confirm whether William H. Ferber appears as a living household member. His presence narrows the death window to post-April 1910; his absence constrains it to before that date and may show his widow's household status. His son Charles and wife Emma are known to have been in Cincinnati Ward 21 in 1910.

Collection 1681000 ('Ohio, Deaths and Burials, 1854-1997') is an aggregated index drawn from multiple sources. It may capture records missed by collections 1307272 and 2128172, particularly church-registered deaths or early county filings. Fallback if the primary Ohio death collections yield nothing.

Collection 2141016 ('Ohio, Hamilton County Records, 1791-1994') holds 1.5M browse-only images of Hamilton County documents including death registers, coroner's records, and other county records not captured by the indexed collections. Valuable if the indexed sources fail; requires image browsing.

Ancestry hosts Ohio death certificates 1908-1953 independently indexed; may capture variant spellings (Ferber/Faerber/Farber) missed by FamilySearch indexing. Search after FamilySearch per free-before-paid principle. Also check Ancestry's city directory collections for years after 1910 to bracket the death window if vital records are absent.

entry.jurisdiction: Cincinnati, Hamilton County, Ohio, United States
entry.rationale: Cincinnati newspapers (Cincinnati Enquirer, Cincinnati Post, Volksblatt) regularly published death notices and obituaries. An obituary would give the death date, place, cause, survivors, and funeral/burial arrangements — potentially the richest single source for this question. GenealogyBank, Newspapers.com (Ancestry), and the Cincinnati Public Library's digitized holdings are the primary access points.

entry.narrative_markdown:
## William Hubert Ferber — Death Date and Place

**Conclusion (Probable):** William Hubert Ferber probably died **11 March 1903** in **Cincinnati, Hamilton County, Ohio**.

### Evidence Summary

**Primary evidence — Hamilton County Death Record (derivative index):**
The Ohio County Death Records collection (FamilySearch collection 2128172, src_001) includes an index entry for "Wm. Ferber" recording a death of 11 March 1903 in Cincinnati, Hamilton County, Ohio (a_003). The entry names his birth year as 1870 in Cincinnati, his marital status as Married, his race as White, and his parents as Gerhard Ferber and Eva Ferber. All identifiers align precisely with William Hubert Ferber (G7JB-YH6): his father Gerhard Ferber (GCD9-9X1, b. 29 Sep 1820, Germany) and mother Eva Engermann Ferber (G7J1-QF2, d. 1 Jan 1872, Cincinnati) are in the FamilySearch tree, and the record was previously attached to G7JB-YH6 with a match score of 0.698. Source classification: **derivative** (index of the original Hamilton County register); information quality: **primary** for death date and place (reported at or near the time of death); evidence type: **direct** (a_001, a_003; pe_001–pe_010).

**Corroborating evidence — 1910 U.S. Census (original):**
The 1910 federal census (src_002) records Emma Ferber as head of household in Cincinnati Ward 21, Hamilton County, Ohio, with marital status **Widowed** (a_012, pe_014–pe_015). William Hubert Ferber is entirely absent from this household, which includes his widow, his father Gerhard (listed as father-in-law), and his son Charles Hubert — all family members who would be expected in his household had he been living (a_022, pe_025). Source classification: **original**; information quality: **indeterminate** for Emma's marital status (self-reported); evidence type: **indirect and negative** with respect to William's death. Emma's widowed status independently corroborates that William had died before April 1910, consistent with — and not in conflict with — the 11 March 1903 county death record. The two sources are genuinely independent: different informants, different institutional origins, different time periods.

### No Conflicts

No conflicts exist between the two sources. The death record's identifiers (name, birth year, birthplace, parents, marital status) are internally consistent and align with all independently known facts about William H. Ferber.

### Why Probable, Not Proved

The primary evidence rests on a **derivative index**, not the original Hamilton County death register. The original register page image (ark:/61903/3:1:S3HT-66TS-SCS) was pursued but is transport-inaccessible at 1.1 MB — the MCP system transport cap was exceeded — and a full-text search pivot returned nil (log_004–log_005). GPS Component 1 is declared met; Components 3–5 are satisfied. However, the GPS Proved standard requires two or more independent **original** sources with primary information. The 1910 census is original but provides only indirect evidence of the death. Until the original register page can be directly examined to confirm the indexed facts, the conclusion stands at **Probable**.

### Path to Proved

If the original Hamilton County death register page (ark:/61903/3:1:S3HT-66TS-SCS) becomes accessible — through a larger transport window or a different access mechanism — and confirms the indexed date and place, the conclusion would advance to **Proved**, provided no contradicting information is found on the original page.

entry.narrative_markdown:
## William Hubert Ferber — Burial Location

**Conclusion (Not Proved):** The burial location of William Hubert Ferber (d. 11 March 1903, Cincinnati, Hamilton County, Ohio) cannot be established from currently searched sources.

### Evidence Examined

The 1910 U.S. Census (src_002) confirms that William's widow Emma Ferber and son Charles Hubert Ferber resided in Cincinnati Ward 21 as late as April 1910 (a_009, a_016), placing the family in Cincinnati at the time of the burial search window. However, no record naming William's burial place has been located.

### Searches Conducted

All FamilySearch-accessible sources for Hamilton County, Ohio burial records were searched and returned negative:
- **Vine Street Hill Cemetery index** (collection 3714673, 1851–1986): no entry for William H. Ferber (log_006)
- **Ohio Deaths and Burials, 1854–1997** (collection 1681000): no matching entry (log_007)
- **Ohio Church and Civil Deaths, 1833–1991** (collection 2373723): no matching entry (log_012)
- **FamilySearch full-text search**, Ohio 1903 newspapers/records: nil (log_005, log_010)

Three high-probability external sources were identified but could not be searched in this autonomous session:
1. **FindAGrave** for Spring Grove Cemetery, Cincinnati — deferred (URL: https://www.findagrave.com/memorial/search?firstname=William&lastname=Ferber&deathyear=1903&location=Cincinnati%2C+Hamilton%2C+Ohio)
2. **Spring Grove Cemetery's own burial database** at springgrove.org — deferred
3. **Cincinnati newspaper obituaries** (Cincinnati Enquirer, Cincinnati Post), March 1903, via Chronicling America and Newspapers.com — deferred

### Family Burial Pattern

A strong family burial pattern exists at Spring Grove Cemetery, Cincinnati: William's mother Eva Engermann Ferber was buried there in January 1872; his wife Emma Becker Ferber was buried there on 10 December 1948; his son Charles Hubert Ferber is also recorded there. This pattern makes Spring Grove Cemetery the most probable burial site for William, but family pattern alone is not genealogical proof of burial location.

### Path to Resolution

An interactive session should search FindAGrave for a Spring Grove Cemetery memorial, query the cemetery's own burial database at springgrove.org, and search Cincinnati newspaper archives (Chronicling America, Newspapers.com) for a March 1903 obituary. Any one of these sources would likely name the cemetery and possibly the undertaker and lot number.
